headline: Discussed Centennial Fund donation appeal, Laptop Connect Program, and library card growth; no major votes taken.
summary: The meeting covered library statistics, the Allegra Goodman literary event, and Friends of the Library activities. The Centennial Ad-hoc Committee reported on the Centennial Fund and plans for a donation appeal. The only vote recorded was approval of the prior meeting's minutes.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the September 14, 2026 regular meeting, with all in favor and none opposed.

decision_evidence.quote: Director Carpenter MOVED to approve the Minutes of the September 14, 2026 Regular Meeting. Seconded by Director Talmadge. All in favor. None opposed. Motion passed.

decision_titles: Minutes of the September 14, 2026 regular meeting
plain_text:
1 
 
MEETING MINUTES OF THE BOARD OF LIBRARY DIRECTORS 
MONDAY, OCTOBER 5, 2026 
Bristol Public Library, 5 High Street, Bristol, CT 06010 
 
ATTENDEES: Valina Carpenter, Eric Frenette, Nicholas Jakubowski, 
Elizabeth Kanachovski, Andrea Kapchensky, Kimberly Ploszaj (Zoom at 
6:35 p.m.), Pina Salvatore, Betty Talmadge, and Council Liaison Steve 
Seymour. 
 
Library Director Deborah Prozzo and Assistant Library Director Scott 
Stanton. 
 
Absent: Danielle Rivard. 
 
Item 1- Call to order 
Chairperson Salvatore called the meeting to order at 6:32 p.m. 
Item 2- Public Participation 
None. 
Item 3- Approval of Minutes 
Director Carpenter MOVED to approve the Minutes of the September 
14, 2026 Regular Meeting. Seconded by Director Talmadge. All in 
favor. None opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Item 4- Communications 
Library Director Prozzo received a communication from Joan Monico 
thanking Joshua from the Reference Dept. for helping her store 
some CDs. She appreciated his highly experienced work ethic.  
Library Director Prozzo was cc’d on a communication from Main 
Street Community Foundation that was addressed to Comptroller 
Diane Waldron. The annual distribution from the Frederick Manross 
Trust Fund was $45,000. It was received on September 25th. The 
revenue account now holds $141,354.63. 
Item 5- Reports and Committee Reports 
 
a. Finance Committee 
No Report. 
b. Property Committee 
No Report. 
c. Policy Committee 
No Report.
2 
 
d. Strategic Planning Committee 
No Report. 
e. Library Director’s Report 
August 2026 Statistics Highlights: Patron visits and website 
visits were both up 5%. Wi-fi sessions were up 30%. Patron 
registrations were up 51%. Our overall circulation was about the 
same as last year.  
Year-to-Date Budget as of 9/28/26: Spending in all departments is 
on track for the first quarter. There was no additional revenue 
logged in since the last report. The next deposit will be done 
this week. There was no interest reported for the Centennial 
Fund. 
Library News: September was National Library Card Sign-up Month. 
We issued 195 new cards. We had excellent community response at 
the Farmers’ Market, the Senior Center Health Fair, and all of 
our school-related outreach events. October is off to a great 
start, too. We have a stack of new registrations. 
The Nutmeg Lit Fest scheduled for Saturday, September 26th was 
canceled due to the weather. We don’t have a new date yet. 
Our literary pop-up event, An Evening with Allegra Goodman, was 
held this past Wednesday. It was a huge success. Thank you to the 
many Friends and staff who made the event run smoothly and thank 
you to the Library Board for allowing us to use Manross Trust 
Fund money. We were allowed to close the library that evening and 
use Funk’s parking lot. We had a great response. The feedback was 
tremendous. People really enjoyed the opportunity to be up close 
with the author. The event was entirely free for the public. The 
majority of attendees were from Bristol however, some came from 
Vernon, West Hartford, Simsbury, Avon, and Burlington. Because it 
was held at night, people who work during the day could attend. 
We had a themed refreshment table which went along with Allegra’s 
latest book, This Is Not About Us. Library Director Prozzo read 
an email from Tina who works at another library: “My mom and I 
thoroughly enjoyed the event with Allegra last night. We were 
immediately welcomed, shown how to navigate the building, and 
greeted at every point. The run of show was clear, the questions 
and content were excellent, and Allegra was warm and funny. Both 
the book sales and autograph line were brilliantly managed and we 
left the event in a fabulous mood. I know how much effort goes 
into library programs and I just wanted to acknowledge everyone’s 
efforts. Thank you for creating a memorable event.” The Board 
should consider holding this type of event on an annual basis. 
October will feature a wide range of programs for children and 
adults at both locations. We will be hosting a Friendsgiving Pie 
Party on Tuesday, October 20th to recognize and celebrate National
3 
 
Friends of the Library Week. We invite all Friends and volunteers 
to the library. 
The winter programming session runs through February. It includes 
Winter Reading programs, which the Friends always support. Scott 
has newsletters and promotional materials out. Today we just 
booked The Golden Scrolls for Bridgerton string music. Sunday 
hours from 1:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. will start on January 10th and 
run through March 28th. 
Director Jakubowski requested data on an infographic showing the 
total number of library cards registered, the number of new 
library card registrations, and the number of cards that have 
expired each month. Library Director Prozzo does not have the 
number of library cards that have expired monthly. The annual 
running total number of cards is close to 17,000. She will add 
the total number of cardholders to the statistics report. The 
strategic planning goal is 20,000. Library Director Prozzo stated 
that one of the things driving the increase in library cards is 
the Laptop Connect Program which we are launching this week. 
Participants must have a current, valid Bristol library card in 
order to be eligible for a free laptop. They must also show proof 
that they are participating in SNAP, HUSKY or Medicare. Don 
Smith, the Computer Lab Supervisor, will be running the one-hour 
“Introduction to Using the Computer” classes. The laptops will 
circulate on a permanent loan. Discussion followed. 
f. City Council Liaison Report 
No Report. 
g. Friends of the Library 
Chairperson Salvatore reported the following: 
The 21st Annual National Friends of the Libraries Week is October 
18th through the 24th. At the Friendsgiving Pie Party on October 
20th, The Friends of the Bristol Public Library will be recognized 
for their financial contributions and volunteer hours which make 
the library a special resource for the community. On behalf of 
the Library Board, Chairperson Salvatore thanked the Friends. She 
will give a card to the Friends signed by the Library Board 
members. 
At the Allegra Goodman Pop-up Literary Event, the Friends did a 
wonderful job providing refreshments, helping in the parking lot, 
and providing other assistance wherever needed.  
The Friends attended four Farmers’ Markets. They had 397 people 
sign up to win a gift card to a local restaurant. They also gave 
out free books. 
The Friends of Connecticut Libraries Newsletter highlighted the 
Godfrey Memorial Library in Middletown which hopes to collect the 
cemetery records of everyone in Connecticut. It is an
4 
 
independent, non-profit library specializing in genealogy in both 
family and local history. It’s open to the public for a fee. 
Carol Ansel is the library director. Her goal is to provide an 
online index of every American from 1607 to date. The library 
contains passenger and immigration lists, databases for various 
newspapers, and MyHeritage database. Assistant Library Director 
Stanton stated that we may have Carol Ansel do a genealogy 
program here in the spring. 
h. Community Engagement Committee 
No Report. 
Director Kanachovski thanked Library Director Prozzo for the 
Allegra Goodman event. She is proud of the Friends and the 
library staff. It was nice that Manross Trust Funds were used for 
the event. The author was a very good speaker. It was a bit more 
intimate than the author luncheons. The question-and-answer 
portion was great. 
i. Centennial Ad-hoc Committee 
Director Carpenter reported that they hit a little bit of a wall 
while researching records from the early ‘90s to determine the 
original intent of the Centennial Fund and what type of fund it 
was. Library Director Prozzo did some further investigating and 
reported the following: The Centennial Fund was formed in 1992. 
At a City Council meeting held on July 13, 1992, council member 
White made a motion to rescind the authorization for the creation 
of a Bristol Library Centennial Account within the general fund 
and to establish an appropriation for the Library Centennial 
Account within the reserve fund for capital and non-recurring 
expenditures. The motion was voted on and passed, but there’s no 
mention of the resolution, which might not have happened. The 
City Clerk’s office could not find the resolution in City Council 
minutes. In 1996, $50,000 was given to the City of Bristol as 
principal to be managed by the city and that was called the 
Library Centennial Account. That’s where the interest is coming 
from. The interest goes into a revenue account which currently 
has about $50,000 in it. There’s also a revenue account for cash 
and check contributions for the Centennial Fund. In addition, 
there’s a new revenue account for contributions made online via 
the donate button on our web page. Then there’s the expenditure 
account that has $143,000 in it. The Library Board can decide to 
do an appropriation. Right now, everything’s just sitting in 
these various accounts. 
Library Director Prozzo suggested that the Centennial Ad-hoc 
Committee consider doing an annual appeal for donations for the 
next hundred years. They can work with Scott to develop some sort 
of statement for the PR. Scott could contact Brian Johnson at The 
Bristol Press. Director Carpenter suggested that the Centennial 
Ad-hoc Committee meet with Scott on Thursday, October 8th at 5:30 
p.m. to discuss ideas and get momentum going before the holidays.
5 
 
Director Jakubowski suggested that Giving Tuesday, which is the 
Tuesday after Thanksgiving, be the target date for launch because 
the majority of fundraising for nonprofits happens between the 
beginning of November and the end of December. The committee will 
work on getting a proposal and/or presentation ready for the next 
Library Board meeting on November 2nd. 
Item 6- Old Business 
  
None.  
Item 7- New Business 
 
None. 
Item 8- Adjournment 
 
There being no further business, Director Frenette made a MOTION 
to adjourn the meeting at 7:09 p.m. Seconded by Director 
Carpenter. All present voted in favor and the meeting adjourned. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
Ruth Vontell 
 
This meeting was digitally recorded.
